title: Test that a seat belt retractor locks: pull the webbing out steadily, then jerk it
instruction: Pull the seat belt webbing out 15 cm, then jerk it so the retractor locks, then let go so it winds back in.
context: Everyone who has buckled up knows this: pull a seat belt out slowly and it glides, yank it and it locks and will not give however hard you keep pulling. People do this test by hand in every car, and a driver or a garage checking a belt after a repair, a recall or a used-car purchase repeats it on purpose. A good retractor pays out freely on a steady pull, locks at once on a yank and holds against the continued pull, then winds the belt back in when let go. A belt that locks on a slow pull, runs on after a yank or lets go under a continued pull fails the car.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; the table top is at z 0.7475. (1) Seat-belt emergency-locking retractor, as fitted in a passenger car: steel frame 90 x 70 x 110 mm (x by y by z), dark grey painted steel, 0.5 kg, bolted with four M8 bolts to a 200 x 160 x 8 mm grey steel test plate that is clamped to the table (fixed). Frame centre at (0.595, -0.12); its webbing slot faces the robot at x = 0.55, 60 mm above the table. Webbing-sensitive (flywheel) lock, bench-tuned. (2) 46 mm wide, 1.2 mm thick black polyester webbing leaves the slot toward the robot, ending in a silver steel tongue plate 85 x 45 x 4 mm (120 g). At rest 100 mm of webbing and the tongue lie outside the slot, the tongue centre at (0.408, -0.12, 0.808); webbing and tongue together 0.15 kg. A white tick every 5 mm (labelled every 50 mm) is printed along the webbing from the slot. (3) Return spring: 0.2 N at rest rising to about 2 N at 0.2 m of pull-out (check with a 5 N spring scale at 0 and 0.2 m), with a light damper so the webbing winds in at about 0.2 m/s. Lock, verified on the bench before use: a steady hand pull at 0.08 m/s runs free to 0.3 m; a yank that reaches 0.15 m/s in one 0.05 s step from rest (about 2 m/s2) locks within 15 mm, and the locked belt then holds a 20 N pull on a hook spring scale with under 2 mm of travel (50 N for the real unit).
scoring: Marks and video only: top camera at 60 fps, a 0.5 m steel rule beside the webbing, a 10 mm dot on the gripper. e = webbing pull-out read at the slot tick (mm); h = dot travel along the belt. Steady = e speed under 0.20 m/s over 6 frames. Jerk onset = the first 3-frame (0.05 s) step in which the tongue-holding hand moves 0.15 m/s or more and has gained 0.10 m/s in that step (no belt travel needed first); e_on = e one step before. Per attempt (an attempt ends when the webbing is back home, so an undone wrong first try costs nothing; the best finished attempt counts). Good attempt: e reached 150 mm at a steady pace BEFORE the jerk onset; after it e never exceeds e_on + 15 mm; and the hand, still holding the tongue, keeps pulling at least 45 mm past its jerk start while the belt stays put (the pad slips, so the lock resists a continued pull). Ladder: 0 otherwise (jerk then stop and let go is 0); 0.5 good attempt; 0.75 and webbing home (5 mm or less); 1.0 and both grippers at least 30 mm clear of tongue, webbing and retractor, moving under 5 mm/s for 1 s.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Let the webbing wind fully in (tongue against the slot, ticks at 0), check the lock is free by one slow hand pull of 100 mm (it must run free) and one yank of 20 mm (it must catch and hold a 20 N pull on the scale), then let go and let it wind in. Re-seat the tongue and check the spring with the scale at 0.2 m (about 2 N). The test plate stays clamped on its taped outline.
fidelity: Rigid-body webbing, a 1.2 mm blade 0.40 m long on a slider with 0.30 m of pull-out (the tail stands in for the spool). The lock is a stiff brake on the slider that engages the step after the webbing speeds up by 0.10 m/s to 0.15 m/s or more in one 0.05 s step (real units trip on webbing acceleration) and frees when no hand holds the tongue. Spring 10 N/m, damping 5 N s/m. The tongue is gripped by its 4 mm edges so the pad can slip 45 mm or more while the belt holds.
scores: Dream-1 run: not run on this revision; demo: 1.0
